risk_if_not_implemented: Without Privileged Access For Vulnerability Scanning Tools, users, services and processes may obtain or retain access beyond authorized need, enabling misuse or escalation. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Excessive or Unauthorized Privilege (R-AC-2), Unauthorized Access (R-AC-4), and most likely increases susceptibility to Malicious Cyber Activity (MT-2), Human Error (MT-9).

compensating_control_1.name: Vulnerability Scanning
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to detect vulnerabilities and configuration errors by routine vulnerability scanning of systems and applications.
compensating_control_1.justification: Vulnerability Scanning (VPM-12) provides vulnerability management that compensates for the absence of Privileged Access (VPM-12.3) by reducing the exploitable attack surface by addressing known weaknesses before they are leveraged. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Vulnerability Remediation Process
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure that vulnerabilities are properly identified, tracked and remediated.
compensating_control_2.justification: Vulnerability Remediation Process (VPM-06) provides vulnerability management that compensates for the absence of Privileged Access (VPM-12.3) by reducing the exploitable attack surface by addressing known weaknesses before they are leveraged. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
